chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the free man marrying the slave woman, or a slave marrying a free woman. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The child would not be enslaved when one of its parents was free. Indeed, it is attached to the free one of the two, whichever of them, be it a father or a mother.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of a child born to one free parent and one slave parent in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'ilqab' (attachment) in mixed-status marriages, establishing that the child inherits the free status of the parent regardless of gender, thereby preventing the child from being enslaved. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic consensus that the freedom of one parent suffices to liberate the offspring, distinguishing it from other schools that may prioritize the father's status. It underscores the egalitarian treatment of maternal and paternal lineage in determining personal liberty within the family structure.
